chunks: As for what was narrated by Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Maḥbūb, from ʿAlī ibn al-Sindī, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Jamīl ibn Darrāj, who said:

I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who becomes junub and forgets to urinate until he performs ghusl, then after the ghusl he sees something. Should he perform ghusl again? He said: “No. It has been pressed out and descended from the passages.”

So this report is to be understood as referring to when he knows that what came out of him after the ghusl was madhy; in that case, repeating the ghusl is not obligatory for him, because what necessitates repeating the ghusl is the خروج of semen, whether little or much.
And what was narrated by Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan al-Ṣaffār, from Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from Aḥmad ibn Hilāl, who said:
I asked him about a man who performed ghusl before urinating, and he wrote: “The ghusl is after urination, unless he was forgetful, in which case he does not repeat the ghusl because of it.”
So it is possible that this report and the one that preceded it are both specific to one who left that due to forgetfulness.

key_terms.الْجَنَابَةُ: the state of major ritual impurity requiring ghusl
key_terms.الْحَبَائِلِ: the passages or channels from which the remaining fluid descends
key_terms.الْغُسْلِ: the ritual bath performed to remove major impurity
key_terms.مَذْيٌ: a lesser sexual fluid whose خروج does not require repeating ghusl in this context
key_terms.نَاسِيًا: forgetfully; the legal exception in these reports is tied to forgetfulness
key_terms.يَبُولَ: to urinate, mentioned here in relation to the proper sequence before ghusl

ai.seo_question: Does ghusl need to be repeated if discharge appears after ghusl done before urinating?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses the ruling of a person in janabah who performs ghusl before urinating and then notices some discharge afterward. The text explains that if the discharge is known to be madhy, ghusl does not need to be repeated, and the cited reports indicate an exception for one who omitted urination out of forgetfulness.
